quarterly_data.signal: NEW CAPACITY AND HYBRID CO-LOCATION OFFER: the PJM bilateral matchmaking process is confidential, but CEO Joe Dominguez: 'You should assume that all of the opportunities we have to add megawatts are being talked to with customers in combination with our existing capabilities.' Dan Eggers: the megawatts Constellation put forward in the interconnect queue were 'a full range, anywhere from uprates on the base load side, to batteries, to peakers'. CEO on the hybrid model (adding batteries and other generation resources at existing operating plants and co-locating a load there): 'We think those hybrid solutions of mixing new capacity resources, existing generation, and co-locating that with load, that's the promise we see going forward.' On uprates: 'We're talking about uprates with clients. That's exciting. You saw that in the Walmart deal.' The RBP 'is one avenue, but it is not the exclusive avenue for customer conversations'. On Illinois' nuclear procurement process: 'We don't have anything separately that we're negotiating with the state of Illinois, to be absolutely clear.'

CEO Joe Dominguez on DATA-CENTER OPPOSITION and existing generation: the public reaction to data centers 'in terms of moratoriums or opposition in places can be strong at times', but 'if we can restart Crane at Three Mile Island and earn overwhelming political and public support, we can certainly earn the public support to build a 21st century data economy in our communities.' Waiting for new power plants before connecting data centers is not what FERC or Secretary Wright is thinking about: 'the bedrock of building out, at least this early phase of the data economy, is going to rely heavily, in my view, on existing generation as it has.'
